title: onprem/airgap: offline bundle vendoring + rke2 (ubuntu-22.04) security patch updates
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Updated offline bundle vendoring for RKE2 on Ubuntu 22.04 with security patch rollups and improved vendoring checksum verification. No user-facing config changes; recommended to apply for air-gapped clusters to address CVE fixes in bundled packages.
description:
Context: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped/on-prem environments using the RKE2 Ubuntu 22.04 distro reported that several CVE fixes (kernel modules and containerd dependencies) were missing from our most recent offline bundle. This PR updates the offline bundle vendoring pipeline to pull the latest patched packages for Ubuntu 22.04, refreshes the RKE2 vendor artifacts, and adds stricter checksum verification tooling to prevent silent corruption during bundle assembly.

What changed: - Bumped vendored RKE2 artifacts to rke2 v1.24.12+redwood.2 (packaged) - Updated Ubuntu 22.04 package snapshots: kernel, containerd, runc, and libseccomp variants to the patched versions recommended by distro advisory - Added a bundle-level SHA512 manifest and verification step in the packager to fail fast on mismatches - Small installer/helm-chart tweak: increase tolerations on control-plane DaemonSet to avoid scheduling on tainted infra nodes during upgrades - Added rollback helper script (tools/onprem/rollback/restore-bundle.sh) that validates bundle signatures before restoring

Checklist: - [x] Update vendored package manifest
- [x] Rebuild offline bundle
- [x] Add SHA512 manifest + verification in packager
- [x] Add unit tests for manifest parser
- [x] Run full airgap integration suite on internal testbed

Why this is safe: The change is limited to offline bundle contents and the packager tooling. Installer/upgrade flow is unchanged except for an additional pre-flight verification step that aborts when checksums fail. Rollback helper is additive. No changes to runtime APIs.

Notes for operators: After merging you'll need to re-generate the public release artifact (airgap-bundle-ubuntu-22.04-2026-02-24.tar.gz) and update the digest file on the downloads page. The new bundle is backwards compatible with existing on-prem control planes; however we recommend scheduling the bundle upgrade during a maintenance window due to kernel package updates.

Related: ENG-4128 (onprem vendoring automation), SUP-2231 (customer security report).

Priya Raman (2026-02-20): Debugging showed the testbed image needed the corresponding kernel headers. Rebuilt bundle with the header packages included; re-ran tests and they passed. Added a test to prevent regressions.
